_about: The sandbox demo scenario (Track A, 2026-10-09). EVERYTHING HERE IS PROPOSED except what a record cites as Alex's: the seed (the prototype's), the two sides' colours and callsign pools (Alex 2026-10-09; data/names/callsigns.json), the map scale and the planes-at-their-own-scale rule (decision demo-baseline). Read by scripts/app/sandbox.gd through scripts/app/sandbox_scenario.gd. Units are in metres on the 5,000 m map (data/sim/turn.json); heading 0 points along +x (east), positive is clockwise on screen. A unit's callsign is either a string or "pool": the first one of its side's and type's pool in data/names/callsigns.json that no earlier unit of the scenario took.

sides._about: Scenario side -> the World's side name (the interface's accent table in data/ui/ui.json knows allies and axis) and the callsign pool (data/names/callsigns.json). side_a is brick red, side_b slate blue (Alex).

units._reason: Player plane 1 (exit criterion 2). Starts a little west of the plateau that begins about 3,200 m east, heading east, so the first turn's carry-on flight crosses a scarp and its trees (criterion 4) in the first screen.
Player plane 2: the heavier type, about 120 m south of plane 1 and a little behind, so two different silhouettes fly side by side.

The AI plane (exit criteria 2 and 7): about 600 m from the players, inside their 800 m sight, flying north-west across their path so the first turn shows all three. It flies on by itself (data/sim/ai_dumb.json).

view._about: How the sandbox shows this scenario. Each can be flipped at run time from the knob panel (F2) or INKWOOD_<KEY> (scripts/debug/debug_settings.gd); these are the values the knobs call "data".

fog._reason: Fog of war is exit criterion 7; on by default so the demo shows it, switchable to compare

plane_px._reason: The assembly brief: planes are drawn at their own scale, a light fighter about 36 px across at zoom 1 whatever the map scale (decision demo-baseline: planes_drawn_at_own_scale). The heavy fighter and the bomber follow in proportion to their size_m

plane_min_px._reason: A light fighter never draws smaller than this on screen, so the planes stay findable when the view is zoomed out to follow a minute of flight; the other types scale with it

start_zoom_max._reason: The opening view frames the players' planes and the first turn's carry-on flight; it does not zoom in past this, so the whole first turn is on screen

start_pad_m._reason: A margin round every plane and its carry-on end in the opening view, so no plane sits on the edge of the free area

start_look_ahead_turns._reason: The opening view frames this many turns of carry-on flight beyond each plane, so the first screen shows where the planes are going

track_sample_s._reason: Tracks (the flown path of each plane, drawn for the whole game) are sampled from each turn's history this often

track_line_px._reason: Track line width on screen; ink in the unit's side colour
